title: Naming the records: West End Blues and Knee Drops
summary: Dance asks about the meaning of titles; Zutty says Knee Drops and Knocking the Jug were named in the studio, and Louis was thrilled to see his name in lights at the Savoy.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well when you did these things the titles you put on, I mean that really didn't mean too much then you know. What did West End Blues mean?
Gee, I don't know. It was Louis' idea.
'Knee Drops.' Just would name them at the studio you know.
Yes, yes. 'muggles' was of course what people were smoking at that time.
'Knocking the Jug.' And you see now that was made in New York.

With Kaiser Marshall. Teagarden, he's on there also. See because that's when Louis from the play at the Savoy. That's when he made those records. He told me, he said, Zutty he said, man, they had my name in lights at the Savoy, you know. Louis Armstrong, you know. And that knocked him out.
Well he sent us a picture from England. Was it the Paladium he was appearing at?
And they had his name outside. He sent us that picture. His name up in the lights.
